clue.text: They don't have to be smart to fool the birds

definitions.text: They don't have to be smart to fool the birds

parts.words: They don't have to be smart to fool the birds
parts.note: smart here means well dressed, not clever: a figure in a field wears old rags yet still keeps crows off the crops

explanation.surface: A remark that you need not be clever to outwit birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like it means intelligent; it means well turned out, and a straw figure in tatty clothes still frightens birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers stand ragged dummies in fields to frighten birds away from seed.

clue.text: Horse fired with enthusiasm in a Western?

definitions.text: fired with enthusiasm in a Western?

explanation.surface: An eager horse in a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' means shot: the revolver named after Samuel Colt is fired in every Western.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male horse; also a revolver brand shot in cowboy films.

clue.text: Don't go-mother is in control

indicators.note: is in places mother's letters inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein controls a horse, so rein means control
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A plea to stay: mum is the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't go' is the definition: stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay put rather than leave.

clue.text: Sort of clothing for resting actors?

definitions.text: Sort of clothing for resting actors?

parts.words: Sort of clothing for resting actors?
parts.note: discarded clothes, with a second reading of actors who are out of a job, a cast that is off

explanation.surface: What out-of-work actors wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Resting is theatre slang for out of work, so the players are a cast that is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-me-down clothes thrown away by their first owner.

clue.text: On top of the bowling

explanation.surface: Something placed atop the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a set of six balls from one bowler is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Means above; also cricket's unit of six deliveries.

clue.text: It contracts to continue one's circulation

definitions.text: It contracts to continue one's circulation

parts.words: It contracts to continue one's circulation
parts.note: the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle squeezes to pump blood round the body

explanation.surface: A newspaper signing deals to keep its sales going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' suggests business deals and 'circulation' newspaper sales; both are about the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the heart's squeezing phase, pushing blood into the arteries.

clue.text: The Daily Worker?

parts.note: the title of an old communist newspaper, reread as someone who works for a daily paper

explanation.surface: The name of a British communist newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Worker was a British Communist paper; read it as a worker on a daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters write for newspapers that come out every day.

clue.text: Order to the non-conformist on the track?

definitions.text: Order to the non-conformist on the track?

parts.words: Order to the non-conformist on the track?
parts.note: an athlete at a race start must put a foot to the mark, and a rebel is told to obey the rules

explanation.surface: An instruction to a rebellious runner.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means conform; literally it is a runner's foot at the start mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to obey rules, from runners placing feet at the starting mark.

clue.text: Vagrant who needs nothing more than a warm place

parts.note: a hob is the warm shelf or cooking top beside a fire
O is the round zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: A tramp who asks for no more than somewhere warm to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing more than' reads as 'only', but it puts O after the hob.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American word for a wandering homeless worker or tramp.

clue.text: New art's seldom produced by great artists

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the next words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A claim that the great painters seldom produced novel art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the ten letters of ART'S SELDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the leading European painters before about 1800, such as Rembrandt.

clue.text: Revolutionary development in naval fire-power

parts.note: revolutionary is taken literally: a rotating gun housing on a warship that spins to aim

explanation.surface: A history note on a radical advance in warship armament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to mean ground-breaking; here it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Warships carry guns in an armoured housing that rotates to train them on targets.

clue.text: Short of shot-guns

parts.note: describes the kind of shotgun whose barrels have been cut down to make it short

explanation.surface: Someone lacking firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' looks like 'lacking'; it describes a shotgun with shortened barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminals cut down shotgun barrels with a saw to make the weapon easy to hide.

clue.text: Minor example of proportional representation

parts.note: proportional representation is an electoral system, but here a small replica in correct proportions

explanation.surface: A small instance of an electoral voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proportional representation' suggests elections; it is a small copy in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature replica built to exact proportions, like a model railway.

clue.text: Do they indicate that crime does pay?

definitions.text: Do they indicate that crime does pay?

parts.words: Do they indicate that crime does pay?
parts.note: plays on the saying that crime doesn't pay, against the Bible verse about the payment due for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A question doubting the saying that crime never pays.
explanation.walkthrough: From Romans 6:23, 'the wages of sin is death': crime does pay, but in death.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bible phrase for death as the reward earned by wrongdoing.

clue.text: He ran a novel criminal class

definitions.text: He ran a novel criminal class

parts.words: He ran a novel criminal class
parts.note: novel is literal: in Dickens's Oliver Twist an old crook trains boys as pickpockets

explanation.surface: A teacher who started an unusual course on crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new'; it means in a novel, Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's villain teaches street boys to pick pockets in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Calm sort of current in S. American river

indicators.note: in places the current's letters inside the name of the river

parts.note: the River Plate flows between Argentina and Uruguay
AC is alternating current, one sort of electric current

explanation.surface: A gentle kind of flow in a South American river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calm' looks like an adjective describing the current; it is the verb meaning pacify.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to soothe or appease them.

clue.text: Put in winning position

explanation.surface: An instruction to set something in first place.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse-race betting, a place means finishing in the first two or three.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down; also a top-few finish that pays out in racing bets.

clue.text: Not an account based on fact

definitions.text: Not an account based on fact

parts.words: Not an account based on fact
parts.note: a made-up story, often with animals, told to teach a moral

explanation.surface: A dismissal of an untrue report.
explanation.definitionFit: A short invented tale, like Aesop's, is a story not rooted in truth.

clue.text: The ship that ended the embargo

indicators.note: ended shows that the name is found at the tail of the next word

explanation.surface: Which vessel brought the trade ban to a close?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ended' looks like 'brought to a close'; the ship's name literally ends the word EMBARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason and his Argonauts sailed the Argo in Greek myth.

clue.text: French girl returns if encored

indicators.note: encored means given again, so the turned word appears twice
returns means the little word if is written backwards

explanation.surface: A French girl comes back if called for an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns IF into FI, and 'encored' repeats it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifi is a pet form of the French female name Josephine.

clue.text: Charming hostess who helped her guests make pigs of themselves

definitions.text: Charming hostess who helped her guests make pigs of themselves

parts.words: Charming hostess who helped her guests make pigs of themselves
parts.note: charming means casting spells: the enchantress in Homer turned Odysseus's men into swine

explanation.surface: A gracious hostess whose guests overindulged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' means using magic, and 'make pigs of themselves' is literal: she changed sailors into swine.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the sorceress on Aeaea transforms visitors into pigs.

clue.text: Plant for a sycophant

explanation.surface: Choosing a plant to suit a flatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant such as ivy; also a toady who fawns on superiors.

clue.text: Green damaged after record stand

indicators.note: after places the scrambled letters behind the record

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of green are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A green item damaged when placed after a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' is the definition, not a verb: an ornamental table piece. 'Damaged' shuffles the colour word, and 'after' puts the record first.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece, a tiered stand for fruit or flowers on a dining table.

clue.text: Oriental nets are cast

indicators.note: cast as nets are thrown suggests these letters being scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Fishing nets being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' fits the nets in the surface but rearranges NETS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things from Asia or the east.

clue.text: Unusual spite shown by the French in a letter

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of spite are put into an odd order

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A letter written with uncharacteristic malice by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' shuffles the spite; 'the French' is the article LE, which ends the word. 'In a letter' is the definition with a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or long letter, like those in the New Testament.

clue.text: A politician in the streets forming impressions

indicators.note: in puts the article and politician inside the abbreviation for streets

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, so streets is STS
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP out on the streets making a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressions' looks like opinions formed; it is marks pressed onto paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamps are marks pressed onto paper with an inked block.

clue.text: Where one is likely to find a rink-manager?

definitions.text: Where one is likely to find a rink-manager?

parts.words: Where one is likely to find a rink-manager?
parts.note: a manager works at a desk, and a manager of a skating rink would be off the ice, splitting the word in two

explanation.surface: A question about where to track down the boss of a skating rink.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as OFF ICE: the rink manager is not on the skating surface but at their desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Managers work in a room set aside for administration.

clue.text: Amount of cloth needed to cover a girl

indicators.note: in a down answer, covering means sitting on top, so the measure goes above the A

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: How much fabric it takes to clothe a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'cover' means placed above: ELL over A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a female first name.

clue.text: Wine that sparkles when it is reflected

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Wine that sparkles when it is reflected', has no parse to ASTI: reversed it reads IT SA ('it's a'), but 'it is' reversed gives SITI; the printed wording may differ and no scan or search confirms it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Wine that sparkles when it is reflected

clue.text: Member of many unions

parts.note: unions here are marriages, not trade unions: someone with several spouses at once

explanation.surface: A keen trade unionist with many memberships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unions' suggests trade unions; it means marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person has more than one spouse at the same time.

clue.text: Ancient Mariner's story brought back by an Arab prince

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the poem is read from end to start

parts.note: Coleridge's poem is The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, rime being an old spelling of rhyme

explanation.surface: Coleridge's sea tale retold by an Arab prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' reverses RIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, a title used in Arab states.

clue.text: University lecturers are in the circulation figures

parts.note: readers are senior lecturers in British universities, ranked just below professors
in meaning fashionable is hip

explanation.surface: Academics featuring in a newspaper's sales numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: A Reader is a British university rank; 'in' means trendy, HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's audience size, its number of people who buy it, is measured in circulation.
